title: How To Handle A High Energy Class
author: Michael Linsin
summary: Linsin frames high-energy students as an asset rather than a liability -- they're primed for learning, fun to teach, and eager to participate -- while acknowledging their tendency toward excessive talking and disruption requires three specific adjustments even from teachers with solid classroom management skills. First, pausing often keeps students focused, slows their racing minds, and builds the discipline of delayed gratification. Second, restraining one's own energy -- limiting pacing, tapping, and constant talking -- transfers a calmer state to students and signals competent leadership. Third, deliberately getting students moving during lessons, through modeling, playacting, or sketching, channels their energy productively and deepens learning more than passive listening would. His overall claim is that these three moves are simply good teaching practice, just needed in higher doses and greater frequency with energetic classes.
points: Timely pauses interrupt a racing mind, improving retention and building the discipline of delayed gratification.
A teacher's own restrained, minimal movement transfers calm to the room and signals competent leadership to students.
Deliberately building movement into every lesson -- modeling, playacting, sketching -- channels excess energy productively before independent work.
None of the three techniques are unique to high-energy classes; they're just standard good teaching applied with greater frequency and intensity.
quotes: Having energetic students isn’t a bad thing. In fact, there are three big advantages: They’re primed for learning. They’re fun to teach. They’re eager to participate.
Timely pausing keeps students focused on you. The momentary silence interrupts their racing mind, slowing it to a more absorbent state and improving interest, understanding, and retention.
Furthermore, it strengthens the discipline to delay gratification, which is a learned ability that can predict academic success.
It also signals to students that you know what you’re doing. They can relax because a competent leader is running the classroom.
Experiencing learning deepens understanding far better and more permanently than simply sending them off after you’re done talking.
The point is that no matter how energetic your class, there are ways to embrace its advantages while curbing the potential negatives.
